question: Can an actual local-cycle reversal, rather than only energy/projector equivalence, lift the two selected native branches isometrically?
frozen_residual: No complex-linear map taking the old global omega eigenmode to the opposite mixed-chirality mode can commute with the unchanged real cycle. The diagonal adapter already fails that demand.
source_operation: Invert each order-three native triangle cycle precisely on faces whose supplied branch sign is negative; keep positive cycles unchanged. This inverse is fixed by C^3=I, not fitted to an observer.
bold_conjecture: The pointed source modes and inherited metric determine a local unitary lift J intertwining C with the signed inverse cycle. For w and conjugate(w), c=<w,conjugate(w)> is nonzero; J w=conjugate(w), J conjugate(w)=(c/conjugate(c))*w. This fixes its action on the complete local two-dimensional space.
rivals: The required c vanishes or local Gram/isometry fails.
Cycle inversion transports but breaks seam energy or canonical pulses.
The two branch-specific inverse adapters close, but repeating the same forward adapter is not an involution.
risky_tests: Verify exact metric unitarity, J C=C_signed_inverse J, C3/L/G/N/energy and all18 canonical projector transport.
Construct the backward lift independently from the opposite selected modes and require it equal J adjoint and recover every coordinate.
Measure J squared rather than silently assume an involution.
scope: Same labelled geometry, source-defined branch signs and exact finite carriers. Inversion is an explicit change of the compared cycle, not proof that unchanged-cycle commutation succeeds or physical time reversal exists.
